title: 1999 AHSME Problem 4
statement: Find the sum of all prime numbers between \(1\) and \(100\) that are simultaneously \(1\) greater than a multiple of \(4\) and \(1\) less than a multiple of \(5.\)

solutions.text:
A number that is \(1\) less than a multiple of \(5\) ends in \(4\) or \(9,\) and one that is \(1\) greater than a multiple of \(4\) is odd. Together these give numbers \(\equiv 9 \pmod{20},\) namely \(9, 29, 49, 69, 89.\)

Among these, only \(29\) and \(89\) are prime, and their sum is \(29 + 89 = 118.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: A number \(1\) less than a multiple of \(5\) has units digit \(4\) or \(9\)
Being also \(\equiv 1 \pmod 4\) forces the number to be \(\equiv 9 \pmod{20}\)
